name: Abbasid Caliphate

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 8.3 million km2 for 800 and 1.0 million km2 for 900 (after the provinces broke away). In 850 Khurasan (Tahirids) and Ifriqiya (Aghlabids) were autonomous but still recognised the caliph, so most of the 800 extent applies (mid); low drops them. The world_800 polygon measures 8.40 million km2.

population.note: Seshat codes 23-33 million for 800 and 9-11 million for the reduced core in 900. 850 sits between: Iraq declining, Egypt rising (HYDE/OWID Iraq 2.5M in 800, Egypt 3.8-4.4M in 800-900). Mid 25 million includes autonomous Khurasan and Ifriqiya; low drops them.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Baghdad 300,000-900,000 (Seshat, disputed) and Samarra, Basra, Fustat, Nishapur, Merv; the most urbanised large state west of China.

activePersonnel.note: Sum of: Samarra central army 20,000-30,000 (Toellner, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ushrusaniyya), half of them Turks; shakiriyya cavalry a few thousand, not more than 5,000 (Kennedy 2001 pp. 201-203, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakiriyya); Baghdad abna and Tahirid forces, frontier (thughur) garrisons in Cilicia and the Jazira, Egypt, Armenia (Bugha the Elder's 852-855 campaign) and the Tahirid army of Khurasan, guessed at 30,000-100,000 together.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Frontier volunteers (mutatawwi'a), Bedouin, Kurdish and provincial levies.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Fleet crews (Egyptian fleet rebuilt after the Byzantine raid on Damietta in 853, Tarsus and Syrian squadrons), engineers, naffatun.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. A salaried army drawn from imported slave soldiers and specific groups; the general population was no longer a military reservoir.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Armoured Turkish ghilman (mounted archers who also fought with lance), shakiriyya and Khurasani cavalry.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: best-equipped cavalry of the Islamic world, lamellar and mail, steppe horses.

training.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: slave soldiers trained from youth.

count.note: Educated guess. Maghariba, Bedouin and horse archers.
Educated guess. Abna and provincial garrison infantry.
Educated guess. Foot archers and naffatun (naphtha throwers).
Educated guess. Irregulars and frontier volunteers on pay.
Educated guess. Traction trebuchets and naphtha engines; Amorium (838) was battered with siege engines.

Educated guess. War galleys of Egypt, Syria and Tarsus. In 853 a single Byzantine squadron of 85 ships raided Damietta unopposed (Bury via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Mutawakkil), so the caliphal navy was weak.
Educated guess. River and coastal craft on the Tigris, Euphrates and Nile.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: capable Turkish generals (Bugha the Elder, Wasif), but command was politicised; al-Mutawakkil was murdered by his own officers in 861.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: rival ethnic regiments (Turks, Maghariba, Ushrusaniyya, abna) loyal to their commanders, not the state.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5: paid professionals, pay arrears a recurrent problem.

weapons.note: Anchor 3-4: composite bows, lances, traction trebuchets, naphtha grenades. audit 2026-10-30: mid 3.8 -> 3.74, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 850 (3.742); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

armor.note: Anchor 3-4: lamellar and mail for ghilman.

fortification.note: Anchor 3-4: walled Baghdad and Samarra, thughur fortresses.

logistics.note: Anchor 3-4: river transport on the Tigris and Euphrates, camel trains, granaries.

communications.note: Anchor 3-4: barid postal relay with stations across the empire.

isr.note: Anchor 3-4: barid officials doubled as intelligence agents.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (via OWID): Iraq 730 = 1,466, Iraq 1000 = 1,307, Egypt 730 = 1,164, Egypt 1000 = 956 (2011 int$). Mid interpolated for 850, weighted towards Iraq and Egypt.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Army pay dominated the budget and its arrears caused the Anarchy at Samarra (861-870).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Textiles, paper (Baghdad mills), metalwork and glass.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Sawad of Iraq and the Nile valley.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Khurasan road, Baghdad-Mecca Darb Zubayda, Roman roads in Syria and Egypt.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Basra, Siraf, Alexandria, Damietta, Tyre, Tarsus, Tunis.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Persian Gulf to China and Indian Ocean trade at its height.

supplyRangeKm.note: Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1) scaled for camel trains, as for the Umayyad snapshot.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. ~0.06-0.15 camels, horses, mules and oxen per inhabitant.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1-1.2: walled cities, desert depth and local supply; population support for the Turkish army in Samarra was poor.

notes: Snapshot = 850, under al-Mutawakkil at Samarra, eleven years before his murder opened the Anarchy at Samarra. Army size is the weakest number: no register total survives for the Samarra period; Toellner's 20,000-30,000 for Samarra and Kennedy's shakiriyya figures are the only modern anchors found, and the provincial and Tahirid forces are guessed. The chronicle figure of 70,000+ for al-Mu'tasim's 838 Amorium army (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Mu'tasim) is noted but not used. Population convention: all lands recognising the caliph, including autonomous Tahirid Khurasan and Aghlabid Ifriqiya (low excludes them); Umayyad al-Andalus and Idrisid Morocco excluded.
